text:
acme-security: Hey Redwood, we saw unexpected decrypts in our Dedicated tenant (acme-tenant) and an IP we don't recognise hitting the KMS endpoint. Can you triage? :worried:

support-ops: Got it — escalating to security. Can you paste the log snippet or timestamps?

acme-security: Here are the KMS logs. `2026-03-20T11:03:12Z decrypt alias/acme-prod principal=arn:aws:iam::123456789:support-service src_ip=198.51.100.23` — about ~17 calls in 10 minutes.

sec-bot: Alert INC-2026-045 created. Rule: kms.decrypt-anomaly. Count=17, affected_tenant=acme-tenant, severity=P2. Routing to sec-oncall. :rotating_light:

lisa-ops: @kevin-r @maria-s please pull audit trail + RBAC changes for acme-tenant since 2026-03-19T00:00UTC. Quick query: `redwood-admin audit query --tenant acme-tenant --since 24h --events "kms.decrypt,rbac.*"`

kevin-r: Running audit query now. Also going to revoke any long-lived tokens for support-service until we confirm. Will update here.

maria-s: Opening runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-anomaly — follow containment checklist. Next steps: 1) snapshot audit logs, 2) freeze RBAC grants to dedicated_admin, 3) rotate keys if unauthorized use confirmed.

support-ops: Notifying customer contacts and scheduling 15:00 UTC bridge. Sending initial acknowledgement to acme-security. :white_check_mark:

kevin-r: Audit results: I see an RBAC grant `role=d edicated_admin` applied to `support-service` at 2026-03-19T22:41Z by user `jenna-t` (internal). That grant allowed KMS Decrypt on alias/acme-prod. Source IPs include 198.51.100.23 and 203.0.113.12.

acme-security: Jenna is internal, but she shouldn't have been able to grant that role in a dedicated tenant. We didn't approve that.

maria-s: Temporary containment: I removed the `dedicated_admin` grant from support-service and disabled all external agent sessions for that principal. Command: `redwood-rbac revoke --tenant acme-tenant --principal support-service --role dedicated_admin` (done).

sec-bot: Action logged to INC-2026-045. Evidence attached: audit-snapshot-1766129800.tar.gz (redacted).

kevin-r: Confirmed decrypts stopped after revocation. No further KMS.decrypt events from those IPs in the last 30m.

lisa-ops: Can we confirm whether any plaintext objects were accessed or exfiltrated? Requesting storage access logs (S3) and VPC flow logs for the same timeframe.

support-ops: Pulling S3 access logs and VPC flow -> `redwood-admin logs export --tenant acme-tenant --since 2026-03-19T22:30 --until 2026-03-20T11:30 --types s3,vpc` — exporting to secure bucket: s3://redwood-incident-exports/INC-2026-045/

acme-security: We also want a signed hash of logs for chain-of-custody.

maria-s: We'll produce a SHA256 manifest and provide the signed manifest with the export. ETA 4 hours.

kevin-r: Root cause initial hypothesis: human error — an internal support onboarding step accidentally granted support-service too-broad RBAC. I'll follow up with the person who made the change and restrict the RBAC change flow.

acme-security: Please confirm any service accounts that accessed customer data and list the exact keys used.

kevin-r: Confirmed service principal support-service performed the decrypts. I've rotated its keys and created a short-lived support token for in-bridge troubleshooting. Rotation commands: `redwood-iam rotate-key --principal support-service --tenant acme-tenant --ttl 1h` (done).

maria-s: KMS key policy for alias/acme-prod temporarily tightened to remove wildcard principals. Added condition `aws:SourceIp` to trusted CIDR list for the customer's VPC until full review.

sec-bot: Timeline updated on INC-2026-045. Severity remains P2.

lisa-ops: Next actions (owner): 1) forensic export (maria-s, 4h), 2) RBAC policy review and approval gating (kevin-r, 48h), 3) post-incident eval + alert tuning (security team, 72h).

support-ops: External comms: Notified acme primary contact that we've contained the activity, rotated keys, and are producing logs. Proposed statement: "No confirmed data exfiltration at this time; investigation ongoing."

acme-security: Thanks. Please also include a list of all RBAC changes for past 7 days and the identity who performed them. We'll need that for our audit.

kevin-r: Done — exported RBAC change log to the incident bucket and redacted internal-only fields per our disclosure policy.

maria-s: Filing follow-up: schedule a joint postmortem with ACME and internal teams next week; action items will include RBAC hardening, KMS alerting thresholds, and stricter change approvals for dedicated tenants.

acme-security: Appreciate the quick response. We'll join the bridge at 15:00 UTC.

support-ops: Bridge invite sent. Closing loop for now, will keep thread updated with artifacts. :people_holding_hands:
